newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol to invest Dfl 500 mln in terminal upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol to invest Dfl 500 mln in terminal upgrade.

text.p: Amsterdam's Schiphol airport will invest 500 million guilders to improve terminal facilities to accommodate rising passenger and cargo traffic, its president Hans Smits said on Tuesday.
From this summer, the central lounge will be expanded and fully renovated and one of the terminal piers will be broadened.
"The passenger will feel more at home at Schiphol (with these measures)," Smits said.

According to provisional figures for 1996, Schiphol remained the fastest growing airport in Europe, it said. Including all transit passengers, the airport handled 27.8 million travellers, up 9.5 percent on 1995. Cargo traffic rose 10.6 percent to 1,081 million tonnes. This resulted in an 11 percent rise in take-offs and landings to a total of 322,000.
The company expects a further seven percent growth in passenger and cargo traffic in 1997.
Legal limits on noise levels restrict Schiphol to 333,000 incoming and outgoing flights, but the airport hopes these can be increased.

Expansion of the terminal will focus on the central lounge, built in 1976, where the first and second floors will be expanded in area by 10,000 square metres, some of which will be occupied by new shops.

The widening of pier D is to accommodate larger planes, such as the Boeing 767-300, which are being increasingly used on European routes. Inside, the pier will be able to hold more passengers and, on the ground floor, will give more room for bagage-handling.
The upgrades are in addition to the existing investment plans, costing about a million guilders per day, the company said in a statement.
Smits added the airport charges would not rise in 1997, but the tariff for transfer passengers would rise by one guilder.
Early this year, the government will decide whether to privatise NV Luchthaven Schiphol.
The Dutch state currently owns 75.8 percent of the airport, with the remainder owned by Amsterdam (21.8 percent) and Rotterdam (2.4 percent) city councils.
